title: Dualizing complexes exist on locally closed subschemes
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra. Work with module sheaves and their ordinary derived categories on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Constructible means locally constant with finitely generated stalks on a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification], [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A dualizing complex on $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ means an object $Q$ of that category such that $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,Q)$ preserves it and every canonical evaluation-transpose map $M\to R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,Q),Q)$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. If a dualizing complex exists on $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, then a dualizing complex exists on $D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ for every locally closed subscheme $T\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here bounded constructible has the same meaning on $T$, and no excellence, dimension bound or cohomological-dimension bound is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.9, p. 313, sentence asserting preservation of existence of a dualizing complex under passage to a subscheme; open case also in the proof of Proposition 7.6.3, p. 311.

proof.text: Fix a dualizing complex $Q$ on $X$ and write $D_X=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,Q)$. First let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open. The localized-site identification [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] and [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] give exact functors $j^*,j_!$. Their termwise derived functors therefore commute with cohomology [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Restriction preserves constructibility [prop-constructible-pullback]. Extension by zero preserves it as well: take the given finite locally closed stratification of $U$, regard those strata as locally closed subschemes of $X$, and add the reduced closed complement, with zero sheaf on it. On the old strata $j_!F$ restricts to $F$, and outside $U$ it is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. Thus $j_!$ and $j^*$ preserve bounded constructible complexes, without enlarging the cohomological interval. In particular $Q_U=j^*Q$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.3, p.311: restriction of a dualizing complex to an open; expanded exactness and stratification argument.

proof.text: Put $D_U=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,Q_U)$. Restriction of derived internal Hom to the slice [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], identified with $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ as in Step 1, gives natural isomorphisms $c_F:j^*D_XF\cong D_Uj^*F$. For $M\in D^b_c(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ apply this with $F=j_!M$. The identification $j^*j_!M\cong M$ follows by restricting the extension-by-zero construction [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Since $D_X(j_!M)$ is bounded constructible by the hypothesis on $Q$, Step 1 now shows that $D_UM$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.3, p.311; expanded internal-Hom restriction argument (Stacks Tag 08JB).

proof.text: The isomorphisms $c_F$ identify $j^*(F\to D_X^2F)$ with $j^*F\to D_U^2j^*F$. Here the maps are the evaluation-transpose maps, not arbitrary isomorphisms: by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] compute Hom using a K-injective target, and use the restriction comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Restricting the evaluation pairing restricts the same composition $(\varphi,m)\mapsto\varphi(m)$; the Koszul symmetry has the same sign before and after restriction. Its transpose is the double-dual map [lem-per-relative-bidual-triangles], so restricting the transpose gives precisely the transpose of that restricted pairing. Apply this to $F=j_!M$. The map on $X$ is an isomorphism by duality; hence its restriction is an isomorphism. Together with Step 2 this proves that $Q_U$ is dualizing.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.3, p.311: the assertion that j^*Q is dualizing, with its canonical biduality map expanded.

proof.text: Now let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed. The inverse images of a finite Noetherian affine cover of $X$ are affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ on $Z$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Quotients are Noetherian because any increasing ideal chain lifts to such a chain in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Thus $Z$ is Noetherian. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. The exact finite direct image and its bounded-below right adjoint $i^!$ are available by [lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom]. Also $i^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ by [lem-kun-04ca]. The latter abelian-sheaf counit is $\Lambda$-linear: it is the counit of the constant-ring module adjunction in the exact-inverse-image node. Apply these identities termwise and pass to derived categories using [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; in particular $i_*$ reflects isomorphisms. It preserves bounded constructibility: extend each stratum of a constructible sheaf on $Z$ to the same locally closed subscheme of $X$, with zero sheaf on $X\setminus Z$. Its restriction to $Z$ is the original sheaf by $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$, and it is zero on the complement by the supported-image assertion of [lem-kun-04ca]. The finite stratification thus witnesses constructibility, and exactness preserves the cohomological bounds. Conversely $i^*$ preserves bounded constructibility by exactness and [prop-constructible-pullback].

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.9, p.313: inheritance under passage to a subscheme, expanded closed case; closed-site support is Stacks Tag 04CA.

proof.text:
Set $Q_Z=i^!Q$, initially an object of $D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. The unit case of [lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom] gives
$$i_*Q_Z\cong R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(i_*\Lambda_Z,Q)=D_X(i_*\Lambda_Z).$$
The sheaf $\Lambda_Z$ is constant of rank one, so is constructible, and Step 4 shows that $i_*\Lambda_Z$ is bounded constructible. Its dual on $X$ is therefore bounded constructible. Apply $i^*$ and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ from Step 4 to conclude that $Q_Z$ is bounded constructible. In particular this argument obtains boundedness of this specific extraordinary inverse image from the dualizing hypothesis; it assumes no general cohomological-dimension bound.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.9, p.313: the closed-subscheme inheritance assertion, expanded using the finite internal-Hom identity of Proposition 5.4.1, pp.291,293.

proof.text:
Write $D_Z=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,Q_Z)$. For every $M\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the same finite internal adjunction [lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom] yields
$$\beta_M:i_*D_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X(i_*M).$$
Its hypotheses hold: $\Lambda$ is finite, both schemes are Noetherian, $i$ is finite, and $M,Q$ are bounded below. The right side is bounded constructible by Step 4 and the hypothesis on $D_X$. Applying $i^*$ as in Step 5 proves that $D_ZM$ is bounded constructible. Thus the same adjunction may also be applied with $D_ZM$ in place of $M$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.9, p.313; finite internal adjunction in Proposition 5.4.1, pp.291,293.

proof.text:
Let $\eta$ denote the canonical evaluation-transpose double-dual maps of [lem-per-relative-bidual-triangles]. By the evaluation--counit normalization in [lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom], the comparison of Step 6 satisfies
$$\beta_{D_ZM}\circ i_*\eta_M
 =D_X(\beta_M)\circ\eta_{i_*M}.$$
To check the equality, transpose both sides under tensor--internal-Hom adjunction, with target $R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(i_*D_ZM,Q)$. On the left, the definition of $\eta_M$ changes evaluation on the double dual into evaluation on $M$ after symmetry; the defining transpose of $\beta_{D_ZM}$ then follows it by the counit $i_*Q_Z\to Q$. On the right, naturality of evaluation changes precomposition by $\beta_M$ into evaluation of $\beta_M$; its defining transpose is the same evaluation on $M$ followed by that same counit. Both transposes are therefore the pairing $i_*D_ZM\otimes^L i_*M\to Q$ defining $\beta_M$, with its factors interchanged by the same Koszul symmetry. The transposition bijection gives the displayed equality. Its right side is an isomorphism because $\eta_{i_*M}$ and $\beta_M$ are isomorphisms. Since $\beta_{D_ZM}$ is an isomorphism and $i_*$ reflects isomorphisms (Step 4), $\eta_M$ is an isomorphism. Steps 5--6 now prove that $Q_Z$ is dualizing.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 7.6.9, p.313: canonical biduality in the closed-subscheme inheritance assertion; evaluation--counit formal calculation.

proof.text: For a locally closed subscheme choose the defining factorization $T\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$, with $i$ closed and $j$ open [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The open subscheme $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and its closed subscheme $T$ is Noetherian by the quotient-chart argument of Step 4. Apply Steps 1--3 to $j$ and Steps 4--7 inside $U$ to $i$. They construct the required dualizing complex $i^!j^*Q$ on $T$. If $T$ is empty its derived category is the zero category and the construction gives its zero dualizing object; the identity open or closed immersion gives $Q$. No reducedness, invertibility of $\ell$, excellence, dimension bound, or uniform cohomological-dimension bound was used. The auxiliary $A$ in the inherited statement plays no role, since the coefficients throughout this assertion are $\Lambda$.
